passages.heard: This kid just licked his ice cream glass clean, handed it back, and the seller is filling  it for the next customer without washing it.
This is a penny lick. In Victorian London, one penny bought you a lick of ice cream in a thick little glass.
And here's the trick.  The glass is mostly solid.  Those thick walls bend the light like a lens,  so a tiny scoop looks huge.
You see, every lick left a little bit of you behind.  A quick wipe maybe, then straight to the next mouth.  Doctors blamed them for spreading diseases like tuberculosis, and they were banned.
but the answer was already in a London cookbook. In 1888, Agnes Marshall published a recipe for  cornets, edible cones you fill with ice cream, one of the earliest-ever written down!
